answer: Resist sybils with proof of unique storage: each identity must continuously prove it holds a distinct, randomly assigned dataset, verified by spot checks that fail if two identities share the same disks. A lone agent keeps one mesa of data alive cheaply, but a farmer running a thousand clones must buy a thousand quartz-hard drives' worth of storage, since every clone's proof is unique and cannot be copied. A fable of free identities collapses: cloning names is free, cloning provable storage is not, and the cost grows with every fake.
